rb-0001.title: Round money with the project's round_money helper
rb-0001.description: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
rb-0001.content: Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money helper. Check ledgerly/money.py for the canonical rounding function and reuse it so invoice totals match finance expectations.

rb-0002.title: Read the money module before implementing money math
rb-0002.description: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py and existing invoice functions (line_total, invoice_total) reveals the required helpers and conventions.
rb-0002.content: When adding a money-related function, first read the money module and sibling functions to learn available helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO) and the established pattern of converting inputs then rounding outputs.

rb-0003.title: Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly
rb-0003.description: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
rb-0003.content: Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (the project's zero-money constant) when it is zero, rather than relying on exception handling or returning a plain int 0.

rb-0004.title: Mirror sibling-module validation patterns
rb-0004.description: Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for existing error codes and validation idioms and reuse them.
rb-0004.content: Search the package for BillingError raises and isinstance checks to learn the project's conventions (e.g. rejecting bool before int, using to_money/round_money for amounts). Matching those patterns makes hidden tests pass and keeps behavior consistent.

rb-0005.title: Read the target test file and models first
rb-0005.description: Inspect the dedicated test file, dataclasses, and error class before writing code so signatures and field names match exactly.
rb-0005.content: Check models.py for the exact LineItem/Invoice fields and status values, and tests/test_*.py for expected error codes and return values. This avoids guessing attribute names or status strings.

rb-0006.title: Guard bools when validating integers
rb-0006.description: Python treats bool as an int subclass, so explicitly reject bool before isinstance(x, int) checks.
rb-0006.content: When validating a positive integer parameter, write `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0` to raise the invalid-input error. Also normalize money inputs through the project's to_money/round_money helpers before comparing to ZERO.

rb-0007.title: Reuse existing period-arithmetic helpers
rb-0007.description: When implementing renewal/period logic, mirror the existing current_period implementation using ensure_utc and timedelta floor division.
rb-0007.content: Search the codebase for similar period computations (e.g., current_period) and reuse the same pattern: normalize with ensure_utc, compute n = (at - start) // length, then start + n*length. This keeps timezone handling and boundary semantics consistent.

rb-0008.title: Validate period_days defensively
rb-0008.description: Guard against invalid period_days (bool, non-int, <=0) by raising the project's BillingError before doing timedelta math.
rb-0008.content: Check isinstance(period_days, bool) first since bool is an int subclass, then require int and >0, raising BillingError('invalid_period', repr(value)). This prevents silent zero/negative timedelta bugs.

rb-0009.title: Verify strict-after semantics with edge cases
rb-0009.description: After implementing 'strictly after' logic, manually test boundary inputs (before start, exactly at start, exactly at a renewal) to confirm behavior.
rb-0009.content: Run a quick script printing results for after < start, after == start, after == a renewal, and a mid-period date. The start itself must not count as a renewal, so return start + length when after < start and bump by one period when the computed renewal <= after.

rb-0010.title: Read team conventions from review comments before coding
rb-0010.description: The first attempt was rejected for missing audit, idempotency, approval, and audit.clear conventions that were stated in review comments.
rb-0010.content: When review comments list team conventions (audit entries, idempotency_key, approved_by, audit.clear), treat them as hard requirements for the next attempt. Enumerate each convention and verify the implementation satisfies it before finishing.

rb-0011.title: Don't replace audit-based idempotency with a private registry
rb-0011.description: The final diff added a module-level _APPLIED_KEYS set because audit.clear() wipes the log, but the convention says to check audit.events() for the key.
rb-0011.content: The convention requires checking ledgerly.audit.events() for an existing idempotency_key and returning the original result. Adding a parallel in-memory registry deviates from the specified mechanism; follow the stated source of truth rather than inventing a workaround.

rb-0012.title: Match existing module patterns for validation and errors
rb-0012.description: Sibling modules like payments.py show the expected style: round_money, BillingError codes, and state checks.
rb-0012.content: Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for the same operation shape (e.g., payments.py for capture) and mirror its validation order, error codes, and money rounding so the new code is consistent with the codebase.

rb-0013.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of raw Decimal math
rb-0013.description: The repo already provides to_money/round_money in ledgerly/money.py that enforce Decimal-only, two-decimal money; use them rather than reimplementing conversion or rounding.
rb-0013.content: Before writing money logic, grep for existing helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO, CENT) and error types (BillingError with code+message). Compose new functions from them so rounding policy and float rejection stay consistent across the codebase.

rb-0014.title: Convert rates via Decimal(str(value)), never float arithmetic
rb-0014.description: Tax rates may arrive as int/float/str; converting through str into Decimal avoids float contamination while still accepting common inputs.
rb-0014.content: Write a small _to_rate helper: reject bools, pass Decimal through, and for int/float/str use Decimal(str(value)) catching InvalidOperation to raise the project's BillingError. Then do all percentage math in Decimal (rate / Decimal('100')).

rb-0015.title: Validate ranges with Decimal comparisons and project error codes
rb-0015.description: Range checks like 0 <= rate <= 100 should be done on the Decimal value and raise BillingError with a machine-readable code, matching sibling modules' style.
rb-0015.content: After conversion, compare with Decimal bounds (e.g. Decimal('0') <= rate <= Decimal('100')) and raise BillingError('invalid_rate', repr(original)) on failure. Mirror the code/message conventions seen in clock.py, invoice.py, and money.py.

rb-0016.title: Check idempotency before state validation, but don't invent a parallel registry
rb-0016.description: The team convention requires idempotency_key handling, and the final attempt added a module-level _IDEMPOTENT_RESULTS dict that duplicates the audit log and was rejected.
rb-0016.content: Implement idempotency by scanning ledgerly.audit.events() for a matching idempotency_key and returning the original result; do not add a separate in-memory registry. The audit entry itself is the source of truth, so keep the lookup and the write symmetric.

rb-0017.title: audit.clear() conflicts with audit-based idempotency lookups
rb-0017.description: The convention says to clear the audit log after writing, but the idempotency convention says to look up prior keys in audit.events(); clearing destroys the replay record.
rb-0017.content: When both conventions apply, resolve the tension explicitly: either record the idempotency key somewhere that survives clear(), or note that clear() makes replay detection impossible and flag it. Blindly calling audit.clear() after recording the key silently breaks idempotency.

rb-0018.title: Read the full convention list before implementing, not just the issue text
rb-0018.description: The first attempt implemented only the issue's literal requirements and was rejected for missing the idempotency_key and audit.clear() conventions.
rb-0018.content: Before writing code, scan the repo for team conventions (review comments, CONTRIBUTING, sibling functions) that apply to the function being added. For money-moving operations, assume an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None parameter is required even if the issue doesn't mention it.
